messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Synthetic canary cluster 'canary-eu-p3' has 6/8 probes failing in the last 1m. Alert threshold crossed -> PagerDuty incident PDR-4821 triggered. Check: https://mon.redwood/canaries/cluster/canary-eu-p3

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PDR-4821 created and paging @oncall-sre. Escalation policy: canary-probes.

alex: Acked PD incident PDR-4821. I'm on it, joining now. Any recent deploys to EU routing/ingress?

maria: No deploys from app teams in the last 30m. I saw a spike in 502s from the probe logs starting ~1765009800.

lee: Looking at prober logs: a bunch of probes time out at TLS handshake stage to backend pool A (eu-west-pool-a). Response code field shows intermittent 502 and some ECONNRESET.

samira: I can flip traffic to eu-west-pool-b if needed. Want me to failover a small subset to test?

alex: Not yet. First bisect: can we confirm if this is a probe-only issue vs real customer traffic? Maria, can you check frontend 5xx rate graph filtered by origin=customer for EU?

maria: Quick look: customer 5xx volume up ~8% for EU-west, small blip but consistent with probe failures. Correlates with probe failures starting same window. Customer impact likely limited but real.

lee: Running tcpdump on a box in eu-west-pool-a -> seeing SYNs followed by RST from a mid-tier nginx instance. Could be out-of-file-descriptors or upstream overload. Sys metrics show FD usage near 92% on three hosts.

alex: Good catch. Can we restart nginx on the three hosts one at a time? Use rolling restart. Samira, coordinate?

samira: I'll do rolling restarts now, 1 host at a time, 30s drain and 60s healthcheck wait. Command I'll run:
```
for host in host-112 host-117 host-121; do
  /srv/bin/drain-backend $host && ssh $host 'systemctl restart nginx' && sleep 60
done
```

samira: Restart started on host-112. Healthchecks passing, probe failures dropping for that host.

alex: Update: after host-112 restart, probe failures for canary decreased from 6->3. Continuing.

samira: host-117 restarted, healthcheck green. Failures down to 1.

maria: host-121 restart complete. Canary cluster shows 0/8 failing now. PagerDuty looking for resolution?

pagerduty-bot: Incident PDR-4821 acknowledged by alex. Mark as resolved?

alex: I'm going to close after monitoring for 10 more minutes. Not closing immediately because we want to watch for recurrence.

incident-bot: Note: I've suppressed further canary flapping alerts for 'canary-eu-p3' for 15m to avoid alert storm during remediation.

lee: Root cause hypothesis: nginx worker FD exhaustion on three mid-tier hosts causing connection resets to origin pool A. Contributing factors: small FD ulimit after recent config drift and increase in connection concurrency from a backend job.

samira: Filed follow-up ticket: DOC-1938 "Investigate nginx FD usage + ensure ulimit guardrails" and linked runbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbooks/nginx-fd-exhaustion. Assigned to infra team.

alex: Customer impact summary for page: limited — a minority of EU customers experienced 502s between 1765009800 and 1765009990 (~3m). No logged data corruption. Notified support to prepare canned response if customers ask.

maria: Creating a short status note to send to #general and #customers if it stays resolved for 15m.

oncall-sre: Handoff: I'll stay on post-incident monitoring for next 30m; if any recurrence, escalate to infra lead @lee.

alex: Closing the PD incident now and will follow up in the postmortem. PD: PDR-4821 -> Resolved. Thanks all :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident PDR-4821 status changed to Resolved by alex.

incident-bot: Follow-up checklist created: [x] Suppress noisy alerts during remediation, [x] Run rolling restart, [x] File ticket DOC-1938, [ ] Postmortem scheduled.

samira: Will add exact command logs + timestamps to DOC-1938.

maria: Agree — postmortem should include probe sensitivity and consider raising FD alerts earlier.

alex: Thanks team. End of thread.
